title: New results keep the old scroll position and selection, and ending a search loses your place in the folder
problem: The folder listing and the search results share one scroll handle per view (`list_scroll`, `grid_scroll`), and the only place they are reset to the top is navigation: `location_changed` (src/finder/mod.rs:916-917). `set_query` (mod.rs:1323-1348), `set_scope`/`set_kind`/`set_search_contents` (1461-1483) and the search response handler (1421-1433) never touch the scroll handles, and `rebuild_rows` only remaps the selection by path (1269). GPUI's uniform_list keeps the pixel offset and clamps it to the bottom of shorter content (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/uniform_list.rs:397-405); the virtual list does the same (gpui-base-0.8.1/src/virtual_list.rs:651-659). Result: (1) scroll halfway down a long folder, press Cmd+F and type: the results open at the same offset, or clamped to the END of a shorter list, showing the worst-ranked hits with the best match off-screen; (2) scroll through results, refine the query: still scrolled. Selection has the same problem: it is cleared only when a search starts (1340-1341); on a refined query the old item stays selected if it still matches, and both Down (src/finder/toolbar.rs:450-459) and Return (mod.rs:1311-1317) select row 0 only `if selection.is_empty()`, so they land on a stale, possibly off-screen item instead of the top hit; Return also selects row 0 without scrolling to it, unlike the Down path. (3) Starting a search clears the folder's selection (1341) and ending it clears again (1336) with the shared scroll left wherever the results were, so Cmd+F, look, Esc drops your place in the folder.
proposal: In src/finder/mod.rs: (1) add a helper `scroll_views_to_top()` doing what location_changed does (`list_scroll.scroll_to_item(0, ScrollStrategy::Top)`, `grid_scroll.scroll_to_item(0, Top)`, plus `strip_scroll.scroll_to_item(0, Center)`). (2) Reset only when the result set on screen changes identity: remember `shown_search: Option<(String, SearchScope, bool, KindFilter)>` (query, scope, contents, kind) and, in the `run_search` completion (1422-1433), when the signature differs from the one last shown, `selection.clear()` and `scroll_views_to_top()` before `rebuild_rows`. (Equivalent: a `reset_results_view: bool` set in `set_query` when the trimmed query changes to another non-empty query and in `set_scope`, `set_kind`, `set_search_contents`.) Re-runs of the same request (indexing retry 1435-1457, Refresh 1202-1203, status poll 1509-1511, settings changes) must not reset. (3) Add `browse_place: Option<BrowsePlace>` holding the selected paths plus the list and grid offsets (read via the `ScrollbarHandle` trait, as src/finder/marquee.rs:156-161 already does). Capture it in `set_query`'s `!was_searching` branch before `selection.clear()`; in the `query.is_empty()` branch restore it after `rebuild_rows` (re-select by path the way `load_listing` does at 1091-1102, then `set_offset`); drop it in `location_changed`. (4) Add `self.scroll_to(0)` next to `select_only(0)` in the PressEnter arm (1313-1316).
original_test_plan: Headless UI tests using a 200-file folder (the existing `long_folder` helper in tests/basics.rs, or 200 `report-000.txt` files written before `Ui::open`): list view, `ui.press("end")` (selects and scrolls to the last row), `ui.click("search")`, `ui.type_text("item")`; read the first result path via `rows_for_test()` and assert `ui.exists(item_id("row", &first))` (rows are virtualized, so existing means on screen; fails today). Scroll the results with `ui.scroll("list", ...)`, type more, and assert the new first row exists. `ui.press("down")`, `ui.press("end")`, click the field, type a refinement, `ui.press("down")` and assert `ui.selected() == [ui.names()[0]]` (today the old last item stays selected). Finally press Escape in the field and assert the folder's last item is selected again and its row (`item 199.txt`) is on screen. Repeat the first assertion in icon view with `item_id("tile", ...)`.
original_risks: The reset must key on the result signature, not on every `run_search`, or the list would jump to the top on each indexing retry. Changes behaviour for anyone who selects a result and then refines the query expecting the selection to stick. `navigate()` calls `end_search` and then `location_changed`, which must still win over the restore. Restoring the folder offset assumes the folder rows are unchanged; if the listing changed meanwhile the offset is simply clamped. Gallery view auto-selects row 0 in `select_first_for_gallery`; make sure the reset and that do not fight.

verifier.claim_check:
The described behaviour is true on every point; the proposal and its test plan need corrections.

Scroll (confirmed):
- `list_scroll` and `grid_scroll` are fields of `Finder` (src/finder/mod.rs:315-321). The folder listing and the results render through the same elements: `uniform_list("list")` with `.track_scroll(&self.list_scroll)` (src/finder/views.rs:614-633) and `v_virtual_list("icon-grid")` with `.track_scroll(&self.grid_scroll)` (views.rs:408-419).
- The only resets to the top are in `location_changed` (mod.rs:916-917). Every other use is `scroll_to(ix)` after a selection move (mod.rs:1892-1902 and its callers).
- `set_query` (mod.rs:1323-1348), `run_search` and its completion (1360-1459), and `set_scope`/`set_kind`/`set_search_contents` (1461-1483) never touch a scroll handle.
- GPUI keeps the pixel offset and only clamps it to the end of shorter content (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/uniform_list.rs:396-405; gpui-base-0.8.1/src/virtual_list.rs:650-658).
- So results open at the folder's offset, and a refined query stays scrolled.

Selection (confirmed):
- `rebuild_rows` only remaps by path (mod.rs:1269, `Selection::remap` at src/model.rs:324-336).
- The selection is cleared only when a search starts (1340-1341) or ends (1336).
- Down in the field (src/finder/toolbar.rs:450-459) and Return (mod.rs:1308-1318) select row 0 only `if selection.is_empty()`, so a result that still matches stays selected, possibly off screen.
- Return's arm has no `scroll_to(0)`; Down's has.
- docs/manual.md:324 says Return moves into the results "selecting the first one", so the stale case contradicts the manual.

Ending a search (confirmed):
- The empty-query branch (1330-1338) clears the selection and rebuilds the folder rows at whatever offset the results had.
- The folder's own selection was already discarded at 1341.

Not intentional and not already handled: docs/manual.md and CHANGELOG.md say nothing about scroll position or selection across queries, and no test in tests/*.rs pins the current behaviour.

Errors in the candidate:
- The primary `shown_search` design never clears the signature when a search ends. "Search x, Esc, scroll the folder, search x again" compares equal and skips the reset. The candidate's own "equivalent" flag variant does not have this hole.
- `ui.scroll("list", ...)` would panic. The id "list" (views.rs:615) is not registered with `.test_support()`; only "list-columns" (views.rs:669-675) and "content" (mod.rs:3279-3280) are.
- The long folder's last item is Roadmap.md, not `item 199.txt` (names sort Budget.csv, item 000..199, notes.txt, Projects, Roadmap.md).
- src/finder/toolbar.rs needs no edit, and CHANGELOG.md is missing from the file list.
verifier.implementation_notes:
All code changes are in src/finder/mod.rs.

1. New state, beside the scroll handles (315-321, initialised near 565):
- `reset_results_view: bool`
- `select_first_on_results: bool`
- `browse_place: Option<BrowsePlace>`, where `struct BrowsePlace { selected: Vec<PathBuf>, view: ViewMode, list: Point<Pixels>, grid: Point<Pixels> }`

2. Use the flag variant, not `shown_search`.
- Set `reset_results_view = true` in `set_query` after the empty-query branch. Line 1325 returns on equality, so reaching that point always means a new non-empty query.
- Set it in `set_scope`, `set_kind` and `set_search_contents` only when `is_searching()`. `run_search` returns early on an empty query, so the flag would otherwise dangle.
- Clear it in the empty-query branch.
- Consume it in the completion closure (1422-1433), after the `search_gen` check and before `rebuild_rows`: `if std::mem::take(&mut this.reset_results_view) { this.selection.clear(); this.scroll_views_to_top(); }`.
- A stale generation returns before consuming, so the flag survives a superseded run.
- Same-request re-runs then never reset. The candidate listed the indexing retry (1451-1455), Refresh (1203) and the status poll (1510). It missed src/finder/tab_bar.rs:63 (`reload_quietly`, after file operations in results), src/finder/batch_rename.rs:231, src/finder/filter.rs:73, and mod.rs:1575, 1597, 1610, 2194.

3. `scroll_views_to_top()`: set the offsets at once through the trait, e.g. `ScrollbarHandle::set_offset(&self.list_scroll, point(px(0.), px(0.)))` and the same for `grid_scroll`.
- Both handles implement the trait (gpui-base-0.8.1/src/scrollbar.rs:102-119 and virtual_list.rs:61-77); src/finder/marquee.rs:156-161 already uses it.
- Do not use `scroll_to_item` here. It is deferred until that list is next painted (uniform_list.rs:372-378, virtual_list.rs:641). The view not on screen would keep the pending jump and later undo the offset restored in step 4.
- The gallery needs nothing: after the clear, `select_first_for_gallery` (1283-1292) selects row 0 and centres the strip.

4. Folder place.
- Capture in `set_query`'s `!was_searching` branch, before `selection.clear()` (1340-1341): the selected rows' paths, `self.config.view_mode`, and both offsets via `ScrollbarHandle::offset`. Do not use `effective_view()`; the query is already set, so Columns reads as List.
- Restore in the empty-query branch after `rebuild_rows` (1337): `take()` the place, map the paths to row indices, call `self.selection.select_items(..)` (src/model.rs:274), then `selection_changed(cx)`.
- If `config.view_mode == place.view`, set both offsets back. In Gallery call `scroll_to(cursor)` instead.
- Do not copy `load_listing`'s `scroll_to(first)` (1100) for list or icons. Its deferred Nearest scroll would replace the restored offset whenever the selected item was off screen when the search began.
- Restoring after `rebuild_rows` also overrides the row 0 that `select_first_for_gallery` just picked.
- This branch covers both exits: Escape in the field (`clean_on_escape`, mod.rs:482, arriving as `InputEvent::Change`) and `end_search`.
- In `location_changed`, set `self.browse_place = None`. `follow_moves` (956) calls it without ending the search.
- `navigate`, `go_back`, `go_forward`, `go_up` and `reveal_in_place` call `end_search` first. The restore's immediate `set_offset` is then overridden by `location_changed`'s clear and deferred `scroll_to_item(0, Top)`, which is the right winner.
- `new_folder` (2778) restores and then `add_and_rename` selects and scrolls to the new folder, which is fine.

5. Return arm (1308-1318).
- Add `self.scroll_to(0)` beside `select_only(0)`.
- This arm reads `self.rows` before the search it just started has answered. Inside the 50 ms debounce it selects row 0 of the old rows, and the arriving reset clears it, leaving the files focused with nothing selected. Today's remap drops it the same way.
- Fix: set `select_first_on_results = true` here when `reset_results_view` is pending. Consume it in the completion after `rebuild_rows` (`select_only(0)`, `scroll_to(0)` when rows are non-empty). Clear it in the empty-query branch.

6. src/finder/toolbar.rs: no change. Once new results clear the selection, the Down handler at 450-459 already selects and scrolls to row 0.

7. Docs.
- docs/manual.md:324 (Searching): add that new results start at the top with nothing selected, and that ending a search returns to the folder's selection and scroll position.
- CHANGELOG.md: add a `### Fixed` entry under `[Unreleased]`.
verifier.test_plan:
Headless UI tests in tests/basics.rs. It owns the private `long_folder` helper (line 13, 200 `item NNN.txt` files written before `Ui::open`, so they are indexed) and already imports `Fixture`, `Ui`, `cmd`, `item_id`, `point`, `px`. Rows are virtualized and `.test_support()` registrations live in GPUI element state (gpui-base-0.8.1/src/test_support.rs:420), so `ui.exists(item_id("row", &path))` means the row is on screen.

1. New results start at the top (list view).
- `ui.click("view-list")`, `ui.press("end")` (selects Roadmap.md and scrolls to the bottom).
- Sanity: `!ui.exists(item_id("row", &fx.path("Budget.csv")))`.
- `ui.click("search")`, `ui.type_text("item")`.
- Read `first` from `ui.read(|f| f.rows_for_test()[0].entry.path.clone())` and assert `ui.exists(item_id("row", &first))`. This fails today.

2. A refined query starts at the top.
- Continue: `ui.scroll("list-columns", point(px(0.), px(-3000.)))`, as basics.rs:764 does. Not "list".
- Assert the first row is gone, `ui.type_text("txt")`, then assert the new first row exists.

3. Icon view.
- Repeat test 1 with `ui.click("view-icons")` and `item_id("tile", &first)` (views.rs:490).

4. Refining drops the old selection.
- Search "item", `ui.press("down")`, `ui.press("end")`, `ui.click("search")` (the caret lands at the end, as tests/finder.rs:259-262 relies on), `ui.type_text("txt")`.
- Assert `ui.selected().is_empty()`. Today the last result is still selected, since every item still matches.
- `ui.press("down")`, then assert `ui.selected() == [ui.names()[0].clone()]` and that the row exists.

5. Ending a search returns to the folder place.
- `ui.click("view-list")`, `ui.press("end")`, `ui.click("search")`, `ui.type_text("item")`.
- `ui.press("escape")` with focus still in the field. One press ends the search there; in the files, Escape clears the selection first (mod.rs:1966-1969).
- Assert `ui.selected() == ["Roadmap.md"]` and `ui.exists(item_id("row", &fx.path("Roadmap.md")))`.

6. Navigation still wins.
- Search, then `ui.go_to(&fx.path("Projects"))`.
- Assert `ui.selected().is_empty()`.

7. Return inside the debounce.
- `ui.click("search")`, then `ui.window(|window, cx| window.input("item", cx))` (no settle; needs `use gpui_kit::test::TestWindowExt as _`), then `ui.press("enter")`.
- Assert `ui.files_focused()` and `ui.selected() == [ui.names()[0].clone()]`.

Existing tests to keep green: `searches_by_name_and_returns_to_browsing` and `type_into_the_search_field_and_down_arrow` (tests/finder.rs:67, 250); `search_field_typing_escape_and_down_arrow`, `search_scope_button` and `scope_bar_controls` (tests/controls.rs:304-390); the search tests in tests/columns.rs. None of them selects a result and then changes the query, scope or kind, or selects in the folder before searching.
verifier.risks:
- The reset must hang on a change of request (the flag), not on every `run_search`. Otherwise the list jumps to the top and loses its selection on the indexing retry, Refresh, the status poll, and the re-runs after file operations, batch rename, filter on/off and settings changes.
- Behaviour change: a result selected before changing the query, scope, kind or name/contents is no longer kept. The preview pane and Quick Look, which follow the selection, go empty, and the gallery jumps to the first result. No test or manual text relies on the old behaviour.
- The restored pixel offset assumes the same view and similar rows. A listing that changed during the search is only clamped by GPUI. A view switched during the search needs the `view` guard, or it gets a stale offset.
- A deferred `scroll_to_item` left on the hidden view's handle would undo a restored offset later; this is why the reset should use `set_offset`.
- Without the `select_first_on_results` flag, Return pressed before the results arrive leaves the files focused with nothing selected. That is not a regression, but it is now deterministic and contradicts docs/manual.md:324.
- Nothing was compiled or run here (read-only review, no cargo). The claim and plan rest on reading the code.
